00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — Maya here from Redwood. I'm joined by Carlos on the engineering side.
00:08 Priya (Nimbus CISO): Hi Maya, hi Carlos. Thanks, we'll keep this tight, we have a lot to cover on SOC2/ISO posture.
00:14 Carlos (Redwood SE): Morning, all. Quick agenda — trust portal access, reports we can share, controls mapping, and then KMS specifics at the end if we have time.
00:25 Ethan (Cloud Ops): Sounds good. We're mainly worried about evidence access and the KMS workflow when we pin to a private deployment.
00:33 Sofia (Compliance): Also RBAC — we need to know if we can restrict access by team and get audit logs for all token activity.
00:42 Maya: Absolutely. To kickoff, quick note on status: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II for the hosted and dedicated planes; ISO 27001 certification is scoped to the control plane and config management. We'll share the redacted reports after today's call.
00:58 Priya: When you say "share" — do you mean a PDF or direct portal access? We prefer portal but also need something to upload to our internal evidence tracker.
01:06 Maya: Both — we can provide PDFs and the Trust Portal read-only link. The portal has artifact attachments, control mappings, and evidence tags. We'll provision a read-only account for your security team.
01:18 Ethan: Good. On the portal, can we export raw audit logs? We want to ingest into our SIEM.
01:26 Carlos: Short answer: yes, you can request a log export. Currently we support S3 exports and direct syslog/forwarding via a connector. The exports include request IDs, timestamps, model namespace, and token counts — but there are redaction rules for PII.
01:40 Priya: What about retention? Nimbus needs 13 months of immutable audit history for regulatory reasons.
01:47 Carlos: Our default is 12 months for the hosted product; dedicated/private can be configured to 24 months. For the hosted plan, we can also set a custom retention via enterprise contract — but that affects storage pricing.
01:58 Sofia: Ok note that down, retention is a must-have.
02:03 Maya: Noted. On KMS — question for Nimbus: are you looking to bring your own key (BYOK) or use Redwood-managed keys?
02:11 Priya: BYOK is preferred. We have strict key custody rules in our policy document.
02:16 Carlos: We support BYOK via AWS KMS and GCP KMS; we also have HSM-backed flows if you want an offline protected key. Integration is mostly about the key import and rotation policy.
02:26 Ethan: Rotation — what default cadence does Redwood use? We need alignment with our 90-day rotation policy.
02:31 Carlos: Default rotation is 180 days for Redwood-managed keys; for BYOK you control rotation. We can propose a rotation seat that triggers a zero-downtime rewrap of envelope keys — I'll capture the steps.
02:44 Priya: How are keys used for inference? Is the model serving layer encrypting in memory or only at rest?
02:51 Carlos: Data-at-rest is encrypted with envelope encryption; in-memory is protected but plaintext exists briefly in process memory for inference. We do not persist plaintext. For the most sensitive workloads we recommend private deployments where you control the KMS and the network boundaries.
03:08 Maya: That's why we offer Private (VPC/air-gapped) installs. Also our Dedicated offering gives isolated GPU pools.
03:15 Priya: We need a controls map — mapping of your SOC 2/ISO controls to our internal control IDs. Can you do that?
03:22 Maya: Yes, we have a controls-mapping template. We'll populate it with annotations about how the control is implemented, evidence locations, and any compensating controls.
03:35 Sofia: Would that include evidence links in the Trust Portal?
03:38 Maya: Exactly. Each control entry in the mapping will point to the artifact in the portal — screenshots, runbooks, test outputs.
03:47 Ethan: A technical question on audit logs: are token-level logs captured? We need token counts and the hashed token IDs for billing reconciliation.
03:55 Carlos: We log token counts and request metadata. We do not log unredacted prompt text in full by default, unless retention/evidence is requested for a specific incident and then it's handled under a legal/evidence process.
04:07 Priya: Hmm, so prompt text is not available — that might be a gap for our incident response playbooks.
04:13 Maya: We can support case-by-case e-discovery with strict access controls and audit of access. We'll add that to the controls doc.
04:22 Ethan: Can you clarify how SSO/SAML works? We need SCIM for provisioning and role mapping so we can enforce least privilege.
04:30 Carlos: We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. Roles in Redwood map to groups in your IdP. For dedicated/private deployments you get additional RBAC granularity — e.g., route-level permissions and key management roles.
04:45 Priya: Do you have separation of duties for key admin vs ops?
04:49 Carlos: Yes — we have an admin role that can manage keys and a separate operator role for day-to-day inference ops. In the Trust Portal we can show role assignments and audit trail.
04:58 Sofia: For evidence — do you have pen test reports and vulnerability scans as part of the portal?
05:03 Maya: We include summary results and remediations; full pen test reports are available under NDA. We'll provide a summary and offer to review with your security team under a separate NDA.
05:15 Priya: Can you walk through an example control mapping for "data encryption key management"?
05:20 Maya: Sure — control ID cloud-crypto-01 maps to SOC 2 CC6.1 and ISO A.10.1; evidence: KMS config screenshot in portal, KMS key policy, rotation logs, and the HSM attestation. For byok we link to the customer key policy doc.
05:39 Ethan: Regarding region pinning — can you pin a tenant to a specific region for both compute and storage?
05:46 Carlos: Yes, for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we currently allow regional tenancy but we need to confirm storage residency for some compliance jurisdictions — we'll call out any exceptions in the spreadsheet.
05:59 Priya: If we need EU-only storage and compute, is that supported?
06:03 Carlos: EU-only is supported with Dedicated or Private. Hosted EU may still have some control-plane metadata in the US depending on service, we'll mark that clearly.
06:15 Maya: We'll annotate the controls mapping with those residency notes so you can pass them to legal.
06:21 Sofia: On the portal, for artifacts, how granular are the timestamps — can we see exact evidence collection times?
06:26 Carlos: Yes, evidence items have ingestion timestamps, collector ID, and checksum. That helps with chain-of-custody requests.
06:35 Priya: Good. A quick question about SLAs — do you have SOC2-related uptime or incident response SLAs tied to the enterprise contract?
06:43 Maya: Yes, SLA for dedicated is in the contract; incident response playbooks and RTO/RPO numbers are included for enterprise customers. We'll put the SLA summary in the portal.
06:52 Ethan: On legal side, we'll need proof of subprocessors and a data processing agreement.
06:57 Maya: We maintain a subprocessors list in the Trust Portal; DPA template we can send — I'll attach that to the follow-up email.
07:05 Priya: Let's talk about evidence access model — can we grant temporary access to auditors outside of Nimbus?
07:12 Carlos: Portal supports time-limited links and auditor roles; you can provision a scoped auditor account with read-only access and expiration.
07:21 Sofia: That would be great for our annual audits.
07:24 Maya: We'll demo that during the follow-up if helpful.
07:28 Priya: On the control gaps, any areas you commonly see as questions from other finance customers?
07:33 Carlos: Usually data residency clarifications, BYOK specifics, and token/prompt retention policies — those are top three. Also sometimes customers ask for FIPS 140-2 HSM specifics.
07:44 Priya: We require FIPS-validated HSM proof for certain keys. Do you support that?
07:49 Carlos: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs via the BYOK/HSM path; we'll note supported HSM vendors and attestation in the mapping doc.
07:59 Ethan: For the KMS workflow during failover — is the rewrap synchronous? Would recovery require key rollover coordination?
08:07 Carlos: The envelope key rewrap is designed to be zero-downtime; you can rotate the envelope without bringing inference offline. We do recommend notifying orchestration teams. I'll include the sequence diagram.
08:18 Maya: Okay, let's go through next steps: we'll share the redacted SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, enable read-only Trust Portal access, and circulate the controls-mapping spreadsheet. Carlos will own the KMS deep-dive.
08:31 Priya: Timeline expectations? We're on a compliance audit window mid-April. We need most artifacts and the gaps called out by end of March.
08:40 Maya: That aligns — we'll aim to get the mapping to you by 2026-03-14 and the reports by 2026-03-12.
08:47 Sofia: One last thing — can we get a statement of who at Redwood will be our ongoing CISO contact?
08:52 Maya: I'll be your primary commercial contact, and Carlos is the technical escalation. For formal CISO-to-CISO touchpoints we can loop in our Head of Security if needed.
09:02 Priya: Perfect. That should do it for high-level. If nobody objects, can we schedule the KMS technical deep-dive next week?
09:09 Ethan: Week of 2026-03-16 works for engineering.
09:13 Carlos: I'll send a Doodle with availability and a tentative agenda — key rotation, rewrap sequence, HSM options, SCIM provisioning.
09:22 Maya: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and portal invite.
09:28 Priya: Thanks.
09:30 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (S-O-O for SSO, K-V cash for KV cache), filler words preserved, some speaker overlap.
